title: HB2746 (2020 Regular): RELATING TO FIREARMS.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Hawaii) (gun-policy Stage 5, Hawaii); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Hawaii text (Introduced, official copy, https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2020/bills/HB2746_.HTM; sha256 bad9143c0735f49f1f1eea8daeb1aa4f093750daf2641c58b8661767135743cc)
provenance.note: As filed. The bill strikes the existing 60-day hunting and 6-month sport-shooting alien permits in (d) and the words 'pistol or revolver' in (g), so the training course applies to any firearm. Struck text is not quoted.

operative_text:
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-2(d)): The chief of police of the respective counties may issue permits to acquire firearms to citizens of the United States of the age of twenty-one years or more, or duly accredited official representatives of foreign nations, or duly commissioned law enforcement officers of the State who are aliens; provided that any law enforcement officer who is the owner of a firearm and who is an alien shall transfer ownership of the firearm within forty-eight hours after termination of employment from a law enforcement agency.
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-2(g)): (1) An approved hunter education course as authorized under section 183D-28; (2) A firearms safety or training course or class available to the general public offered by a law enforcement agency of the State or of any county;
